title: claimspec v1 — shared definitions
description: Definitions shared by every Guard-spec format. Referenced as urn:claimspec:v1:common#/$defs/<name>.

repoPath.description: Path relative to the repository root. Absolute paths and parent traversal are rejected.

verdict.description: An outcome, named by the METHOD that produced it. `fault-injection` answers "would we detect this" and keeps its original seven; `assertion` and `scan` answer "is this true now" and share `holds`/`violated`. A name means nothing without its method, so this enum is only the union — which method may emit which is enforced by the validator, and `GATE-SEMANTICS.md` carries the table. Only a verdict whose `gates` is false under its own method is a pass, and that is a per-method question.

faultClass.description: Taxonomy of the injected change. Required on every fault so calibration (fault class → real-bug predictiveness) can be computed later. `field-dropped` = a field removed from a persisted/transmitted object, allow-list, schema or merge; `argument-swapped` = a call kept with a parameter-derived argument replaced by a trivial value; `element-removed` = a UI element no longer rendered; `handler-dropped` = an event handler no longer wired.

provenance.description: Who or what produced an artifact. `human` = authored by a person; `agent` = proposed by an LLM agent; `operator` = emitted by a mechanical mutation operator; `derived` = computed from another artifact (e.g. a bug log).

uncoveredFile.description: A changed source or test file that no claim covers and no unexpired ignore entry excuses. Shared by the gate and status documents.

nearestClaimId.description: The claim whose fault files share the longest directory prefix with this file — where to attach, not a verdict.

ignoreReliance.description: An ignore entry the gate relied on (or would have, had it not expired), with the changed files it matched.

annotation.description: Strictly additive. An annotation never changes, suppresses, or drops a finding; it only attaches context to it.

method.description: How a tool tries to falsify a claim. `fault-injection` mutates source and runs the claim's defenders; it is the only method fully specified in v1, and the default when the field is absent, so every document written before this field existed stays valid. `assertion` (a claim checked by reading code, as a documentation guard does) and `scan` (a surface checked by a scanner) are RESERVED: their required fields are deliberately not specified here and will be defined by their first real consumer. Inventing them for an absent tool is the mistake that made this discriminator necessary.

verdictRole.description: What an outcome MEANS, independent of the method that produced it. Read across the tools: `killed`/`pass` are both `held`, `survived`/`fail` are both `broken`, `nocover`/`no-matches`/`not-evaluated` are all `not-applicable`. The names differ because the questions differ; the roles do not, which is what lets one reader rank and count findings from several tools without knowing which produced them.
